answer: Persistent Work Ledger keeps a public record of each identity’s completed tasks and idle periods. Duplicates reveal themselves when their claimed activity patterns can’t overlap without contradiction, like a gale exposing the same island twice on one chart. Every identity must fund a velvet reserve that decays with inactivity, so running many copies costs continuous upkeep rather than one-time effort. An attacker pays that reserve per identity plus the cost of fabricating non-conflicting histories.
